long_biography.plain_text:
Mortgage entrepreneur Malcolm Watkins initially trained in dentistry, then abandoned that direction after deciding he preferred sales. Returning from overseas travel, he spent a year clearing farmland to repay his debts. Selling flowers and fax machines preceded his move into financial services.

At Australian Finance Group, he helped develop electronic exchanges between brokers and lenders. Through the Trident Project, three broker groups and four banks adopted LIXI standards for transmitting home-loan applications. AFG also helped develop standards for application-status messages and commission payments. Watkins pressed lenders to automate more of their loan-processing systems.
